newsitem.title: EGYPT: Cairo bourse rises on housing firm gains.
newsitem.headline: Cairo bourse rises on housing firm gains.

text.p: Brisk trading in the housing sector helped push Egyptian shares upwards on Sunday despite some slippages in the popular milling sector, brokers said.
The Capital Market Authority (CMA) all-share index gained 2.87 points to close at 281.61 while turnover was an above-average 41.08 million pounds ($12.1 million).
Heliopolis Housing and Development was the day's most active share and its biggest gainer.
The stock, which surged on Thursday in heavy trade, jumped again more than 11.67 percent, or 35.00 pounds, to 335.00.
Broker Walid el-Kholi of El-Rashad Securities told Reuters he thought speculators were behind most of the trade.
Trading was also heavy in blue-chip Medinet Nasr Housing and Development, another housing firm which has also witnessed a recent boost in its price, but the firm shed 4.00 pounds to close at 284.00.
Amriyah Cement was the second most active share, with shares worth 4.63 million changing hands. It finished 0.60 up at 76.00 pounds.
Popular milling firms were hit by profit-taking and some share prices slipped in spite of brisk trade.
East Delta Flour Mills fell 0.05 to end at 50.00, while Upper Egypt Flour Mills closed unchanged at 69.60.
But Central and Western Delta Flour Mills added 2.00 pounds to close at 83.50.
The CMA index for openly traded firms rose to 430.91 from 425.89 points on Thursday while the index for rarely traded "closed" firms rose to 196.06 from 194.23.
